hypotheses.reasoning: notif-worker was processing notifications.outbound normally until 18:05:48. Then it crashed on one message, msg-364842 at offset 371126, with a RangeError (stack overflow) in expandReferences. That points to a self-referencing or very deeply nested payload. Every restart (#1975, #2032, #2129, #2291, with growing backoff) tries the same offset again and crashes the same way, so the consumer never moves past it. That causes the CrashLoopBackOff and the rising lag.

notif-worker v1.8.8 rolled out at 18:02:55, about 3 minutes before the first crash. But the worker processed many batches without trouble after the rollout, and every crash is on the same single message. So a new code bug is less likely, though the new version may have made expandReferences less tolerant of this payload.

verdict.recommendedAction: Move msg-364842 (offset 371126) to a dead-letter queue, or advance the consumer offset past it, so notif-worker can drain the backlog. Then add a recursion depth limit or cycle detection to expandReferences, catch errors per message and route failures to the DLQ, and find out which producer sent the cyclic or deeply nested payload. If the bug turns out to come from v1.8.8, consider rolling back.
